questions.question_text:
A vertical mast $OT$ is supported by two cables anchored at ground points $A$ and $B$.
Cable $AT$ is $38\text{ m}$ long with an angle of elevation to the top $T$ of $47^{\circ}$.
Anchor point $B$ is on horizontal ground $25\text{ m}$ from base $O$.
What is the angle of elevation of $T$ from $B$, to the nearest degree?

options.why: Used $\cos 47^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 47^{\circ}$ to find the height $OT$, calculating $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{38\cos 47^{\circ}}{25}\right) \approx 46^{\circ}$.
Inverted the tangent ratio as $\frac{25}{38\sin 47^{\circ}}$, calculating the complementary angle at the top of the mast.
Divided the slant cable length $38$ directly by $25$ rather than finding the vertical height $OT = 38\sin 47^{\circ}$ first.

questions.question_text:
From point $P$ due south of a vertical tower $OT$ of height $90\text{ m}$, the angle of elevation of $T$ is $27^{\circ}$.
From point $Q$ due east of the tower, the angle of elevation of $T$ is $38^{\circ}$.
What is the distance $PQ$ across the ground, to the nearest metre?

options.why: Added the two ground distances $OP + OQ$ directly instead of applying Pythagoras' theorem $PQ = \sqrt{OP^2 + OQ^2}$.
Multiplied by tangents ($90\tan 27^{\circ}$ and $90\tan 38^{\circ}$) instead of dividing by tangents to find ground lengths.
Used the average angle $32.5^{\circ}$ in a single triangle, calculating $90/\tan 32.5^{\circ}$ instead of finding and combining the two ground distances.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOP\text{:}$
$OP = \frac{90}{\tan 27^{\circ}} = 176.634\dots\text{ m}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOQ\text{:}$
$OQ = \frac{90}{\tan 38^{\circ}} = 115.194\dots\text{ m}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta POQ\text{:}$
$PQ = \sqrt{\left(\frac{90}{\tan 27^{\circ}}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{90}{\tan 38^{\circ}}\right)^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{31199.9\dots + 13269.8\dots}$
$= 210.8\dots\text{ m}$
$= 211\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
A rectangular block has dimensions $10\text{ cm} \times 8\text{ cm} \times 6\text{ cm}$ (height $6\text{ cm}$).
What is the angle that the space diagonal makes with the base plane, to the nearest degree?

options.why: Used the side edge length $10\text{ cm}$ instead of the base diagonal $\sqrt{10^2+8^2} = \sqrt{164}\text{ cm}$, calculating $\tan^{-1}(6/10) \approx 31^{\circ}$.
Used the width edge length $8\text{ cm}$ instead of the base diagonal, calculating $\tan^{-1}(6/8) \approx 37^{\circ}$.
Calculated $\sin^{-1}(6/\sqrt{164})$ using the base diagonal as hypotenuse rather than as adjacent side.

questions.question_text:
A right pyramid has a square base of side length $18\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $15\text{ cm}$.
Find the angle of inclination of a triangular side face to the base plane, to 1 decimal place.

options.why: Used the full base side $18\text{ cm}$ instead of the distance from centre to edge ($9\text{ cm}$), giving $\tan^{-1}(15/18) \approx 39.8^{\circ}$.
Used the half-diagonal $9\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$ to calculate slant edge angle instead of face inclination.
Inverted the tangent ratio, calculating $\tan^{-1}(9/15) = 30.96^{\circ} \approx 31.0^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Distance from base centre to face midpoint: } OM = \frac{18}{2} = 9\text{ cm}$
$\tan\theta = \frac{15}{9} = \frac{5}{3}$
$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)$
$= 59.036\dots^{\circ}$
$= 59.0^{\circ}$

questions.question_text:
A vertical radio mast $OT$ of height $60\text{ m}$ stands on level ground.
From its base $O$, station $A$ is on a bearing of $070^{\circ}\text{T}$ and station $B$ is on a bearing of $160^{\circ}\text{T}$.
The angles of elevation of the mast top $T$ measured from stations $A$ and $B$ are $31^{\circ}$ and $41^{\circ}$ respectively.
Find the distance $AB$ between the stations, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Added the two horizontal ground distances $OA + OB = 99.9 + 69.0$ instead of using Pythagoras' theorem on the perpendicular bearings.
Subtracted $OB$ from $OA$, calculating $60/\tan 31^{\circ}-60/\tan 41^{\circ}$ instead of combining the perpendicular ground distances using Pythagoras' theorem.
Multiplied the height $60\text{ m}$ by each tangent, calculating $60\tan 31^{\circ}$ and $60\tan 41^{\circ}$, then combined the two resulting lengths using Pythagoras' theorem.

questions.question_text:
From point $X$ due south of a flagpole, the angle of elevation of the top is $36^{\circ}$.
From point $Y$ due east of the flagpole, the angle of elevation is $48^{\circ}$.
If the distance between $X$ and $Y$ along level ground is $72\text{ m}$, find the height $h$ of the flagpole, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Formed the equation using tangents rather than cotangents, solving $h\sqrt{\tan^2 36^{\circ} + \tan^2 48^{\circ}} = 72$.
Averaged the two elevation angles to calculate $72\tan 42^{\circ}/2$.
Omitted the square root when solving for $h$, calculating $72 / (\cot^2 36^{\circ} + \cot^2 48^{\circ})$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Let }F\text{ be the foot of the flagpole.}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta XFY\text{:}$
$FX = h\cot 36^{\circ}, \quad FY = h\cot 48^{\circ}$
$(h\cot 36^{\circ})^{2} + (h\cot 48^{\circ})^{2} = 72^{2}$
$h = \frac{72}{\sqrt{\cot^{2} 36^{\circ} + \cot^{2} 48^{\circ}}}$
$= \frac{72}{\sqrt{1.894427\dots + 0.810727\dots}}$
$= \frac{72}{\sqrt{2.705154\dots}}$
$= 43.7\dots\text{ m}$
$= 44\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
Two observers $A$ and $B$ are $100\text{ m}$ apart on level ground.
A tower $OT$ is due north of $A$ and due west of $B$.
The angle of elevation of $T$ from $A$ is $22^{\circ}$, and the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $055^{\circ}\text{T}$.
Find the height $h$ of the tower, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Used $100\sin 55^{\circ}$ instead of $100\cos 55^{\circ}$ to calculate the ground distance $OA$.
Multiplied $100\tan 22^{\circ} = 40.4\text{ m}$ without resolving the horizontal triangle $\Delta OAB$.
Found the base distance $OA = 100\cos 55^{\circ} \approx 57\text{ m}$ but forgot to multiply by $\tan 22^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Since }O\text{ is due north of }A\text{, }\angle OAB = 55^{\circ}\text{.}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta OAB\text{:}$
$OA = 100\cos 55^{\circ} = 57.3576\dots\text{ m}$
$\text{In vertical right-angled }\Delta TOA\text{:}$
$h = OA\tan 22^{\circ}$
$= 57.3576\dots \times \tan 22^{\circ}$
$= 23.174\dots\text{ m}$
$= 23\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
Two boats are observed from the top $T$ of a vertical lighthouse $OT$, $100\text{ m}$ above sea level.
Boat $X$ is on a bearing of $040^{\circ}\text{T}$ from the lighthouse and at an angle of depression of $20^{\circ}$.
Boat $Y$ is on a bearing of $130^{\circ}\text{T}$ from the lighthouse and at an angle of depression of $14^{\circ}$.
Calculate the distance $XY$ between the boats, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Added the two ground distances, calculating $100/\tan 20^{\circ}+100/\tan 14^{\circ}$ instead of using Pythagoras' theorem.
Subtracted the ground distances, calculating $100/\tan 14^{\circ}-100/\tan 20^{\circ}$ as though the boats were in the same direction from the lighthouse.
Multiplied by tangents instead of dividing, calculating $\sqrt{(100\tan 20^{\circ})^{2}+(100\tan 14^{\circ})^{2}}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle XOY = 130^{\circ} - 40^{\circ} = 90^{\circ}$
$\text{The angles of elevation from the boats equal the angles of depression.}$
$OX = \frac{100}{\tan 20^{\circ}}$
$OY = \frac{100}{\tan 14^{\circ}}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta XOY\text{:}$
$XY = \sqrt{OX^{2} + OY^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{\left(\frac{100}{\tan 20^{\circ}}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{100}{\tan 14^{\circ}}\right)^{2}}$
$\approx 486\text{ m}$
